bullets.headline: September payroll employment increased by 29,000 and unemployment held at 4.2%; July and August payroll gains were revised lower by a combined 60,000.
bullets.context: Stable unemployment and 3.0% year-over-year private-sector wage growth provide some income support, but weak job creation and downward revisions could increase caution among lower- and middle-income buyers.

bullets.headline: August personal income rose 0.2%, disposable income rose 0.3%, and consumer spending increased 0.9%.
bullets.context: Income and spending growth indicate continued consumer capacity to support durable-goods purchases, although the 4.1% saving rate suggests limited cushion for households facing elevated vehicle prices and financing costs.

bullets.headline: U.S. regular gasoline averaged $4.465 per gallon, up from $4.085 on August 24.
bullets.context: The increase raises operating costs and may shift consideration toward more fuel-efficient cars, hybrids, and smaller crossovers, while potentially reducing discretionary spending available for vehicle purchases.

bullets.headline: Cox Automotive raised its full-year U.S. new-vehicle sales forecast to 16.1 million units; September sales were expected to rise 6.5% year over year, while August inventory stood at 2.68 million units and 73 days’ supply.
bullets.context: Resilient demand and improving credit availability are supportive for industry volume, but inventory is becoming more constrained in affordable segments; Cox also reported an average new-vehicle listing price of $49,486 in August, limiting accessibility for payment-sensitive buyers.

bullets.headline: Federal Reserve raised the federal-funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00%.
bullets.context: Higher policy rates can keep auto-financing costs elevated and constrain monthly-payment affordability, with the greatest exposure among rate-sensitive shoppers and higher loan-to-value transactions.
